static_traits.name: Chen Jie
static_traits.social_status: Has a few close friends to talk to, but friendships are affected by concealing an important hobby
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; has not yet received psychotherapy; no history of similar psychological problems
static_traits.language_features: Emotionally tense but Positive attitude; clear expression, well-organized; capable of self-Reflection and cooperating with exploration and exercises

basic_info.main_problem: I feel uneasy about my passion for clay modeling, fearing others' judgment, which leads me to hide this hobby and feel ashamed of it.
basic_info.core_demands: I realize this insecurity and Fear of being judged are affecting my mental health, preventing me from Freely enjoying my hobby; I hope to express myself freely and embrace my hobby.
growth_experiences: About a year ago, a friend made a disparaging comment about my clay-modeling hobby, and since then I began feeling shame and insecurity; stress levels were high at the time, and I gradually formed the view that 'others will see my hobby as childish or geeky'. Afterwards I increasingly tended to hide this hobby, no longer participating publicly, even feeling guilt and shame when doing it privately. Since then, whenever thoughts about clay modeling arise, I avoid discussing or participating, long-term affecting emotions and relationships.

core_beliefs: Others will look down on me because of my hobbies
Expressing the true self brings judgment and humiliation

special_situations.event: A year ago a friend made disparaging comments about my clay model hobby
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If someone belittles my hobby, it means it is indeed childish, others will all see me that way too
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Hides the hobby, reduces sharing work with others, avoids related topics
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will laugh at me, thinking I am a 'geek' or childish

special_situations.event: Whenever thinking of sharing the clay-model hobby with others
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I talk about or show this hobby, others will think I am strange, childish, or wasting time
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Done only in private, actively avoids discussion and self-exposure in social situations
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will think I am weird and laugh at me

special_situations.event: When with friends, becomes aware that oneself is concealing this part of life
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I do not hide, relationships will be damaged, they will look down on me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Continuing to conceal and avoid, Displacing attention to other topics
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If they knew the real me, they would not accept me

special_situations.event: Feeling creativity and passion weakened by insecurity in Work
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my hobby is not recognized, then my creative passion is not worth showing publicly either
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Maintains basic work performance but suppresses expressive enthusiasm and related creation
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: My creativity is not worth being seen, better not to show it publicly

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be seen and accepted with genuine interests (Freely expressing self and creativity)
core_conflict.fear: Fears being mocked, judged, and rejected with damaged relationships
defense_goal: Self-protection through hiding and avoidance, reducing the risk of being negated by the outside world

object_relations.self_representation: A self easily mocked and devalued

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When talking about 'publicly sharing hobbies' in counseling or invited to do reality-testing exercises
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Equates openness and self-exposure with being judged and humiliated (transference: projecting past experiences of being devalued onto the current interaction)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Cautious tone, lowering self-exposure; downplaying real feelings, turning to safer topics (such as work), expressing 'I'll think about it more', avoiding being forced; the counselor needs to invite them to gradually elaborate the experience in a low-arousal, empathic, and normalizing manner.

manifestations: Hiding the hobby due to fear of others' judgment, Restricted self-expression
Avoids showing true interests in social settings
Having close friends but not yet sharing real unease and important hobbies
outcomes: Emotional alienation and reduced sense of being understood

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: Presumes others will see one's hobby as childish or geeky
Before obtaining evidence, pre-judging that others will mock or belittle oneself

positive_force: Having a few close friends as potential support
Stable work performance, with sustained artistic creation ability
Proactively seeking counseling, possesses motivation to change and self-Reflection ability
negative_force: High sensitivity to and fear of others' judgment (mind reading, overgeneralization)
Strong sense of shame; tends to conceal and avoid self-exposure
Self-worth excessively dependent on external evaluation (external validation)

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding discussing or showing the clay-modeling hobby in front of others, accompanied by shame and insecurity
antecedent: Thinking about sharing hobbies with others or showing work
Being asked about hobbies when with friends
target_behavior.core_reason: The friend's disparaging remarks Reinforced the Fear of negative evaluation and catastrophic Anticipation, forming cognitive biases of mind reading and overgeneralization, thus using avoidance for Self-protection
target_behavior.function: Avoiding unwelcome stimuli (mockery, criticism, being belittled), reducing the immediate experience of Anxiety and shame
target_behavior.consequence: Tense relationships with friends, emotional estrangement; Declining creativity and passion; feeling guilt and shame when doing it privately, further solidifying the avoidance cycle
